name: Rani ki Vav
summary: An eleventh-century subterranean stepwell on the old bank of the Saraswati, commissioned in memory of Bhima I. Seven levels of galleries carry hundreds of sculptures, many depicting the avatars of Vishnu.

name: Adalaj Stepwell
summary: A five-storey stepwell begun under Rana Veer Singh and completed in 1499 for Queen Rudabai, its pillars and niches blending Hindu, Jain and Islamic ornament.

name: Dada Harir Stepwell
summary: Built by Bai Harir Sultani in Asarwa, a long stepped corridor of five storeys ends at an octagonal well; inscriptions in Sanskrit and Arabic record its founding.

name: Modhera Sun Temple
summary: A temple to Surya built under Bhima I, with a carved assembly hall and the Surya Kund, a great stepped tank ringed by miniature shrines.

name: Champaner-Pavagadh
summary: Sultan Mahmud Begada's capital at the foot of Pavagadh hill, with mosques, fortifications and water-retaining structures; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004.

name: Dholavira
summary: A Harappan city on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch, laid out around rock-cut reservoirs and channels that captured seasonal streams; inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2021.

name: Lothal
summary: A Harappan port town whose large brick basin is often interpreted as one of the earliest known dockyards.

name: Uparkot Fort
summary: A hill fort above Junagadh enclosing Buddhist caves, a mosque and two wells cut deep into the rock: Adi Kadi Vav and Navghan Kuvo.

name: Aina Mahal
summary: An eighteenth-century palace in Bhuj built for Rao Lakhpatji, celebrated for its mirror-work hall and the craftsmanship of Ram Singh Malam; damaged in the 2001 earthquake.

name: Ajrakhpur
summary: A village of Khatri block-printers who resettled here after the 2001 earthquake, practising Ajrakh resist printing with natural indigo and madder.

name: Nirona
summary: A Kutch village known for Rogan painting with castor-oil paste, hand-hammered copper bells and lacquerware.

name: Patan Patola
summary: Double-ikat silk patola woven by Salvi families in Patan; warp and weft are resist-dyed separately before weaving, so a single sari can take months.

name: Chand Baori
summary: One of India's deepest stepwells: thirteen storeys of criss-crossing flights of steps on three sides of a square shaft, with a royal pavilion on the fourth.

name: Agrasen ki Baoli
summary: A 60-metre-long stepwell near Connaught Place with 108 steps, linked by tradition to Maharaja Agrasen though its masonry suggests the Tughlaq or Lodi era.

name: Toorji ka Jhalra
summary: An eighteenth-century stepwell in rose-red sandstone built by a queen consort of Maharaja Abhay Singh, cleared and restored in the 2010s.

name: Hampi Stepped Tank
summary: A symmetrical stepped tank of finely dressed schist blocks in Hampi's Royal Enclosure, part of the Group of Monuments at Hampi.

name: Golden Temple
summary: The principal gurdwara of the Sikhs, founded by Guru Ram Das and completed under Guru Arjan, with its gold-covered sanctum set in the Amrit Sarovar.

name: Golconda Fort
summary: A hilltop citadel of the Qutb Shahi sultans, known for its acoustic engineering, granaries, water systems and the diamond trade of the Deccan.

name: Charminar
summary: A four-minaret monument built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1591 to mark the founding of Hyderabad; its upper storey contains a mosque.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
summary: A vast temple complex around the shrines of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, with fourteen gopurams covered in painted stucco sculpture and the Golden Lotus Tank.

name: Kondapalli
summary: A craft town near Vijayawada known for brightly painted Kondapalli toys carved from soft poniki wood, a GI-tagged tradition.

name: Konark Sun Temple
summary: A monumental chariot-form temple to Surya with 24 carved wheels and seven horses; the main shrine is now roofless. Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1984.
description: The Sun Temple at Konark was built in the mid-13th century under King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, about 35 km from Puri on the Odisha coast. Its surviving audience hall and subsidiary shrines are conceived as the chariot of Surya, with giant stone wheels, horses and dense bands of sculpture. The principal tower has collapsed, leaving the sanctum open to the sky, but the scale and carving of the complex remain exceptional. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1984.

name: Tawang Monastery
summary: The largest monastery in India, founded in the 17th century by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso, overlooking the Tawang Chu valley.

name: Shaniwar Wada
summary: The fortified residence of the Peshwas in Pune, entered through massive gates; its palace was destroyed by fire in 1828, leaving the stone walls and foundations.

name: Ajanta Caves
era_label: Buddhist rock-cut caves, 2nd century BCE–6th century CE
summary: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist caves in a horseshoe gorge, with monasteries, prayer halls and painted murals that are among the oldest surviving Indian paintings. Inscribed in 1983.

name: Sanchi Stupa
summary: The Great Stupa and its surrounding monasteries, begun under Ashoka and expanded with carved gateways and railings over the following centuries. Inscribed in 1989.
description: The Buddhist complex at Sanchi grew around the Great Stupa, traditionally begun by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Under the Satavahanas the stupa was enlarged and enclosed by a stone railing, and its four carved gateways were added around the 1st century BCE. Monasteries, votive stupas and temples continued to be built on the hill through the early medieval period. The site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1989.

name: Bastar Dhokra
summary: A living bell-metal casting tradition of Bastar, using the lost-wax method to make figurines, jewellery and ritual objects; Kondagaon is a major centre.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
summary: The temple complex of the Chandela capital, famed for tall Nagara-style spires and dense bands of sculpture; the Kandariya Mahadeva is its largest surviving temple. Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1986.
description: Khajuraho was the ceremonial capital of the Chandela Rajputs, who built a large group of sandstone temples there between roughly 950 and 1050 CE. About twenty temples survive, arranged in western, eastern and southern groups. The western group is the best known: the Kandariya Mahadeva rises through a sequence of roofed halls into a tall curvilinear spire covered with sculpture, while the Lakshmana and Vishvanatha temples show the same Nagara vocabulary at smaller scale. The carvings range from deities and attendants to courtly processions and mithuna couples. The complex was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

name: Victoria Memorial
summary: A white-marble memorial to Queen Victoria in the Maidan, designed by William Emerson in Indo-Saracenic style and opened in 1921; it now houses a museum and gallery.
description: The Victoria Memorial was proposed after Queen Victoria's death in 1901 and paid for by public subscription and contributions from princely states. William Emerson designed the building in an Indo-Saracenic idiom, combining Mughal details with European planning, and it was constructed in Makrana marble between 1906 and 1921. The central dome rises above a formal garden, and the interior now holds a museum of colonial-era paintings, documents and objects. It is a major Kolkata landmark but is not a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Qutub Minar
summary: A red sandstone and marble minaret begun by Qutb al-Din Aibak around 1199 and completed by Iltutmish, standing at the centre of the Qutub complex. Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1993.
description: The Qutub Minar is a tapering victory tower and minaret in Mehrauli, Delhi, begun around 1199 by Qutb al-Din Aibak and completed by his successor Iltutmish. Its five storeys alternate between red sandstone and marble, with carved bands and balconies, and it rises to about 73 metres. The surrounding Qutub complex includes the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, the Alai Darwaza gate and the Iron Pillar. The minaret and its monuments were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

name: Taj Mahal
summary: The white-marble mausoleum Shah Jahan built for Mumtaz Mahal at Agra between 1632 and 1653, set in a formal charbagh garden above the Yamuna. Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1983.
description: The Taj Mahal was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as the tomb of his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631. Construction began at Agra in 1632 and was largely complete by 1653. The complex combines a monumental white-marble mausoleum, a great gateway, a mosque and assembly hall, and a formal charbagh garden aligned with the Yamuna river. Its surfaces carry inlaid stone flowers, calligraphic bands and carved screens, and the mausoleum is flanked by four minarets. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
